questionsToConsider: Which fields does your invoicing or delivery process actually need, and which are nice to have?
Do you need a tax or VAT number from business customers before you can bill them?
Is a postal address necessary, or only a city and country?
Who on your team owns the customer record once it arrives, and who updates it later?
guide.howToUseResponses: Treat each response as the first version of the customer's record. Copy it into whatever system you bill or deliver from, or export the responses to CSV and import them in a batch. Check the marketing answer before adding anyone to a mailing list, and honour the preferred contact method and time from the first call onwards. The notes field is where access details and special requests hide, so make sure it reaches whoever serves the customer.
customizeSteps: Remove the address fields you never use, or drop the state line if you only serve one country.
Rewrite the consent wording so it names what you actually send and how often.
Send the link as part of your welcome email, or embed it on the page customers land on after they buy.

faqs.q: What should a customer information form include?
faqs.a: Name, email and phone, an address if you deliver or invoice, and how the customer prefers to be contacted. Business customers also need a company name and a billing contact.

faqs.q: Do I need consent to email customers?
faqs.a: For marketing, in many countries yes. This form asks separately and records a clear yes or no, while service messages about their account go out regardless.

faqs.q: Why ask whether the customer is a business?
faqs.a: Businesses need extra details such as a tax number and an invoice address. Asking first means individuals never see those questions.

faqs.q: Can I export customer information to a spreadsheet?
faqs.a: Yes. Every answer appears in your dashboard and can be exported to CSV, with one column per field.
